children: U.S. crude oil inventories and diesel stocks are expected to have inched slightly lower last week, according to a survey by The Wall Street Journal.

Commercial crude stocks are seen falling by 200,000 barrels to 426.2 million barrels in the week ended Sept. 25, according to the average estimate of five analysts and traders. Three expect a decline and two predict an increase, with estimates ranging from 2 million barrel draw to a 1.9 million barrel build.
Gasoline inventories are expected to rise by 300,000 barrels to 206.3 million barrels, with forecasts ranging from a 1.1 million barrel drop to a 2.8 million barrel increase.

Stocks of distillate fuel, mostly diesel, are expected to have fallen by 200,000 barrels to 107.2 million barrels. Estimates range from a drop of 1.7 million barrels to an increase of 1 million barrels.

Refinery capacity use is seen falling by 0.6 of a percentage point to 93.4%, according to the survey. Forecasts range from a 0.1 percentage point decline to a 0.9 percentage point decline. Two analysts didn't forecast refinery runs.
The inventory data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration is scheduled for release at 10:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday.

This was corrected at 2:05 p.m. ET. Refinery capacity use is seen falling by 0.6 of a percentage point to 93.4%, according to the survey. The original version misstated that refinery capacity use is seen falling by 0.5 of a percentage point.
Correction to Analysts Anticipate Lower U.S. Crude Oil Stockpiles

Refinery capacity use is seen falling by 0.6 of a percentage point to 93.4%, according to the survey. "Analysts Anticipate Lower U.S. Crude Oil Stockpiles" published at 1:39 p.m. ET misstated that refinery capacity use is seen falling by 0.5 of a percentage point in one reference.
